Well, this whole situation has been going on for about 11 months now. It all started right around the time my sister's health suddenly took a turn for the worse, and I had to step in and start coordinating all her care. 

Which, let me tell you, coordinating care is practically a full-time job in itself. It reminds me of when I was trying to organize the annual summer picnic for my office. But yes, to answer your question, it's been about 11 months of them deliberately keeping me in the dark since I had to take over her care.

We took him out to this lovely Italian restaurant to celebrate, the one downtown with the red checkered tablecloths. I had the eggplant parmesan, and it was divine. The portion was so huge I had to take half of it home in a little box. I had it for lunch the next day, and it was almost better leftover, you know how the flavors just meld together in the fridge? I always put a little extra parmesan cheese on top when I reheat it... \n\nBut anyway, no, I don't think anyone is using cameras or secret devices or anything like that. It's just the staff being difficult and trying to keep me away, no gadgets involved.\n\nDoctor: For how long have you been certain that people are deliberately keeping information from you about your sister’s care?\n\nPatient: Well, this whole situation has been going on for about 11 months now. It all started right around the time my sister's health suddenly took a turn for the worse, and I had to step in and start coordinating all her care. \n\nWhich, let me tell you, coordinating care is practically a full-time job in itself. It reminds me of when I was trying to organize the annual summer picnic for my office. I was the one who had to call all the caterers, and you wouldn't believe how hard it is to find a good potato salad. Everyone thinks they make the best potato salad, but most of them just use way too much mayonnaise. I finally found this little deli on 4th Street that puts a hint of Dijon mustard in theirs, which gives it this wonderful tang. I ended up ordering three large tubs of it. We had the picnic at Centennial Park, down by the lake. It's such a lovely spot, except for the geese. You really have to watch where you step because of the geese. One of the junior accountants, bless his heart, wore brand new white sneakers and stepped right in a massive pile of goose droppings. He spent half the afternoon trying to scrape it off with a stick... \n\nBut yes, to answer your question, it's been about 11 months of them deliberately keeping me in the dark since I had to take over her care.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe the staff are actively plotting together against you?\n\nPatient: Plotting together? Well, I don't know if they have secret meetings in a dark room, but they're definitely working together to push me out. I'm here because for months now, I've been seeing the exact same pattern. My sister's appointments get moved without anyone telling me, the bills show up wrong, and people conveniently \"forget\" to call me back. \n\nSpeaking of forgetting to call back, I tried to get a plumber out to the house last week because the guest bathroom sink was draining so slowly. I called three different places, left voicemails, and not a single one called me back. It’s impossible to find good help these days. I finally had to go under the sink myself and unscrew that little U-shaped pipe—the P-trap, I think it's called? It was absolutely disgusting, just full of hair and soap scum. I had to use an old toothbrush to clean it out. I kept that toothbrush specifically for cleaning grout, you know, because the bristles get perfectly into the little lines between the tiles. I use this homemade mixture of baking soda and vinegar, it bubbles up and works so much better than those harsh chemical sprays. Plus, it doesn't give you a headache. I get terrible tension headaches if I smell bleach for too long...\n\nBut anyway, whenever I point out these \"mistakes\" with my sister's care, everyone just brushes it off. They say, \"Oh, it's just an administrative error,\" or \"We're just short-staffed.\" But I know better. Even when everyone says it's just mistakes, I know they're actively keeping information from me and trying to push me out of making decisions for her. It's too consistent to be an accident.\n\nDoctor: If the staff showed you clear proof that the appointment changes and billing errors were routine mistakes, would you accept that?\n\nPatient: Clear proof? Well, I don't know what they could possibly show me that would change my mind at this point. I mean, they can print out all the spreadsheets and memos they want, but I know what I'm seeing. I've been seeing the exact same pattern for months now—her appointments getting moved around, the bills showing up completely wrong, people conveniently forgetting to call me back. \n\nIt’s like when I was trying to get a refund for that blender I bought at the department store last month. Someone—and I won't name names, but she sits at the front desk and spends half the day looking at shoes online—ordered three boxes of blue pens instead of black. Blue pens! Who uses blue pens for official documents anymore? It looks so unprofessional. I had to call the vendor and sort the whole thing out. The vendor is this lovely man named Gary, he's been our rep for years. He always asks about my cats. I have two, a tabby named Oliver and a calico named Penelope. Penelope is such a picky eater, I have to buy this special grain-free food that costs an absolute fortune, and even then, she'll only eat it if I sprinkle a little bit of chicken broth on top. Not the low-sodium kind either, she won't touch that. It has to be the regular kind. \n\nBut anyway, no, people don't usually say I have trouble getting to the point. I think I'm very clear when I speak.\n\nDoctor: Outside of your sister’s care, do you currently believe other people are deliberately trying to harm, deceive, or exclude you?\n\nPatient: No, no, nothing like that. I still keep my home in order, I pay my bills on time, and I do my job. \n\nActually, speaking of my job, I just organized the most beautiful retirement party for one of our senior accountants, Martha. It's not too sweet, you know? Some places just dump powdered sugar into shortening and call it frosting, but this is real Swiss meringue buttercream. It takes forever to make because you have to heat the egg whites and sugar over a double boiler until it reaches exactly 160 degrees, and then you whip it until the bowl feels cool to the touch before you even think about adding the butter. If the butter is too warm, the whole thing turns into soup, and if it's too cold, it gets all curdled and lumpy. I watched this whole documentary on baking science once when I couldn't sleep. It was fascinating how humidity affects flour absorption...\n\nBut anyway, people might think I'm too focused on what's happening with my sister's care, but I'm not falling apart or acting strangely in other parts of my life. You really have to feed it at the exact same time every day, and keep it at the right temperature. I kept mine on top of the refrigerator because it’s just a little bit warmer up there...\n\nBut no, to answer your question, I wouldn't accept it. Because even when everyone stands there and says it’s just routine mistakes, I know the truth. They’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of making decisions for her. No piece of paper they show me is going to change what I know is happening.\n\nDoctor: Do people often tell you that you go off on tangents or have trouble getting to the point when you talk?\n\nPatient: No, I don't think so. I mean, nobody's ever come right out and said that to me. I've always thought of myself as a pretty good communicator, actually. You have to be, in my line of work. Managing an office, you're constantly talking to people, making sure everyone is on the same page. \n\nLike just last Tuesday, we had this massive mix-up with the office supply order. Someone—and I won't name names, but she sits at the front desk and spends half the day looking at shoes online—ordered three boxes of blue pens instead of black. Blue pens! Who uses blue pens for official documents anymore? It looks so unprofessional. I had to call the vendor and sort the whole thing out. The vendor is this lovely man named Gary, he's been our rep for years. He always asks about my cats. I have two, a tabby named Oliver and a calico named Penelope. Penelope is such a picky eater, I have to buy this special grain-free food that costs an absolute fortune, and even then, she'll only eat it if I sprinkle a little bit of chicken broth on top. Not the low-sodium kind either, she won't touch that. It has to be the regular kind. \n\nBut anyway, no, people don't usually say I have trouble getting to the point. I think I'm very clear when I speak.\n\nDoctor: Outside of your sister’s care, do you currently believe other people are deliberately trying to harm, deceive, or exclude you?\n\nPatient: No, no, nothing like that. It's really just the situation at the facility with my sister. Outside of dealing with her appointments and trying to get straight answers from those people, everything else is perfectly fine. I still keep my home in order, I pay my bills on time, and I do my job. \n\nActually, speaking of my job, I just organized the most beautiful retirement party for one of our senior accountants, Martha. She's been there for thirty years. We got her this gorgeous sheet cake from that little bakery on 4th Street—the one with the green awning? They do the most incredible buttercream frosting. It's not too sweet, you know? Some places just dump powdered sugar into shortening and call it frosting, but this is real Swiss meringue buttercream. It takes forever to make because you have to heat the egg whites and sugar over a double boiler until it reaches exactly 160 degrees, and then you whip it until the bowl feels cool to the touch before you even think about adding the butter. If the butter is too warm, the whole thing turns into soup, and if it's too cold, it gets all curdled and lumpy. I watched this whole documentary on baking science once when I couldn't sleep. It was fascinating how humidity affects flour absorption...\n\nBut anyway, people might think I'm too focused on what's happening with my sister's care, but I'm not falling apart or acting strangely in other parts of my life. I'm just trying to protect her, that's all.\n\nDoctor: Have you taken any action to protect your sister because you were certain the staff were deliberately keeping information from you?\n\nPatient: Well, I've had to be more firm, certainly. I mean, when you know something isn't right, you can't just sit back and let it happen, can you? So yes, I've brought it up at family meetings. But honestly, those have become so tense lately. My brother just sits there looking at his watch, and my sister-in-law gets this pinched look on her face. It's exactly the same look my third-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable, used to get when someone didn't know their multiplication tables. She was a very strict woman, Mrs. Gable. She wore these heavy tweed skirts even in the middle of May, and she always smelled faintly of mothballs and peppermint. I actually started keeping peppermints in my desk at work because of her. The little red and white striped ones, you know? They're quite good for settling the stomach. \n\nI've needed them at work recently, to be honest. I’ve had a few... uncomfortable conversations there, too. I suppose I’ve been pressing people harder about routine mistakes than I used to. Like with the filing system—if something is misfiled, I need to know *why*, not just that it was an \"accident.\" But I'm still managing all my responsibilities! It’s just... I've noticed it has started to affect how people respond to me. They get quiet when I walk into the breakroom. The breakroom really needs a new microwave, by the way. The one we have now heats everything unevenly. I tried to warm up a bowl of tomato bisque the other day—I made it from scratch over the weekend, roasted the tomatoes with garlic and thyme—and the edges were boiling but the center was ice cold. You really need a microwave with a proper turntable for soup... \n\nBut yes, I've had to take action. I'm just trying to make sure things are done correctly, whether it's for my sister or at the office.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe your coworkers are deliberately treating you differently because they’re against you?\n\nPatient: Against me? Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I don't think it's anything malicious. They're just... well, I think they just don't like being held to a high standard, you know? It's certainly not some kind of plot against me. \n\nTake Sarah, for instance, in payroll. She's not against me at all. We actually used to carpool on Thursdays before she bought that new hybrid car. It's a lovely shade of silver, though. I've always liked silver cars, even if they do get terribly dirty in the winter. The salt on the roads around here just coats everything. My father had a silver sedan when I was growing up, and I remember every Sunday morning he would be out in the driveway with a bucket of soapy water and a sponge, washing off the road salt. He used this special wax—Turtle Wax, I think it was called? It came in a little green tub and smelled strongly of coconuts. I always loved that smell. It reminds me of the beach. No, my coworkers aren't against me. I ended up digging the whole thing up and planting hostas instead. Hostas are so much more reliable, especially in the shade under that big oak tree I have. Though the slugs do love them. You have to put out little shallow dishes of beer to catch the slugs. They just crawl right in... \n\nBut anyway, yes. I know what I'm seeing with my sister's care. They can call it \"mistakes\" all they want, but I know they are intentionally keeping things from me.\n\nDoctor: Have you made a formal complaint or accusation against the staff because of what you believe they’re doing?\n\nPatient: Well, no, I haven't filed any formal complaints yet. It was only $8.99, but it's the principle of the thing, isn't it? I spent forty-five minutes on hold listening to this awful, tinny elevator music. It sounded like a pan flute being played underwater. I don't understand why companies can't just play classical music while you wait. A little Mozart or Vivaldi would be so much more soothing. They were so thin, almost like crepes, and she’d serve them with lingonberry jam. You can’t really find good lingonberry jam in the regular grocery stores around here. You have to go to that specialty market downtown, the one next to the old movie theater. \n\nBut no, I haven't made a formal accusation against the staff. I've just been keeping a very close eye on things myself.\n\nDoctor: Do you think there is any chance at all that you might be mistaken about the staff deliberately keeping information from you?\n\nPatient: Mistaken?
